The matching sides are $6$ cm and $9$ cm, which are not equal.

The transformation is a translation.

The image has been turned a quarter turn to point in a different direction, but it is not back-to-front.
The transformation is a rotation.

options.text: their centres are at the same point
options.why: The centre only fixes the circle's position, not its size — circles about the same centre can have different radii.

options.text: the radius of one equals the diameter of the other
options.why: The diameter is twice the radius, so that circle would be twice as wide as the first, not congruent to it.

questions.solution_text:
A circle's size is completely fixed by its radius.
Two circles are congruent exactly when their radii are equal.

options.text: No, because their matching angles are not equal
Yes, because all their matching sides are equal

options.text: Yes, because they have the same perimeter
options.why: Equal perimeters do not make figures congruent — shapes with the same perimeter can have completely different angles.

options.text: No, because a rectangle can never be congruent to a parallelogram
options.why: A rectangle is itself a parallelogram, and two identical rectangles are congruent — the reason here is the unequal angles, not the shape names.

questions.solution_text:
The matching sides are equal, but the rectangle's angles are all $90^{\circ}$ and the parallelogram's are not.
No translation, reflection or rotation can move one exactly onto the other, so the shapes are not congruent.
